categories.name: Platform-facing routes
categories.findings_markdown:
Router registration (control-plane/internal/api/api.go:114-125, stdlib http.NewServeMux, Go 1.22+ pattern routing):

| Method | Path | Handler | file:line |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | /v1/verify | handleVerify | api.go:132 |
| POST | /v1/verify/bulk | handleBulkSubmit | api.go:216 |
| GET | /v1/jobs/{id} | handleJobStatus | api.go:272 |
| GET | /v1/jobs/{id}/results | handleJobResults | api.go:312 |
| GET | /healthz | handleHealthz | api.go:355 |
| GET | /readyz | handleReadyz | api.go:361 |

No /v1/quote, /v1/run, /v1/report, or /v1/describe exist anywhere in the Go tree (grep across control-plane/internal and control-plane/cmd returns zero hits besides an unrelated regexp.QuoteMeta call in smtp_stage.go). This module implements ITS OWN verb set: a synchronous POST /v1/verify (single-address, inline verdict) and an async bulk pipeline POST /v1/verify/bulk -> GET /v1/jobs/{id} (progress) -> GET /v1/jobs/{id}/results (paginated verdicts). There is no separate 'quote' verb; cost/feasibility is not exposed at all (see category 7) and there is no polling verb named 'describe' or 'report' - job status/results ARE the poll mechanism.

POST /v1/verify - request struct verifyRequest (api.go:127-130):
```
type verifyRequest struct {
    Email  string `json:"email"`
    Policy string `json:"policy,omitempty"`
}
```
email required (400 {"error":"email is required"} if empty/absent); policy optional, must equal the wired default policy key or 400 {"error":"unknown policy"} (api.go:163-166). Body capped at 1<<16 bytes (64KiB) via http.MaxBytesReader (api.go:149).

Response on 200: verdict.Response (verdict/verdict.go:17-29), the frozen 'Door 1' contract:
```
type Response struct {
    APIVersion     string                 `json:"api_version"`
    Status         vocab.Status           `json:"status"`
    Reason         vocab.Reason           `json:"reason"`
    Confidence     int                    `json:"confidence"` // int 0-100
    Recommendation vocab.Recommendation   `json:"recommendation"`
    Email          string                 `json:"email"`  // echoes RAW input
    Domain         string                 `json:"domain"` // normalized; "" if not extractable
    Flags          map[string]bool        `json:"flags"`
    Signals        map[string]any         `json:"signals"`
    Meta           Meta                   `json:"meta"`
    Raw            map[string]any         `json:"raw"` // null when no engine consulted
}
type Meta struct {
    RequestID         string  `json:"request_id"`
    CheckedAt         string  `json:"checked_at"` // RFC3339 UTC
    LatencyMS         int     `json:"latency_ms"`
    Policy            string  `json:"policy"`
    PolicyVersion     int     `json:"policy_version"`
    VerifierIP        *string `json:"verifier_ip"`
    NodeID            *string `json:"node_id"`
    EngineVersion     *string `json:"engine_version"`
    ConfigFingerprint *string `json:"config_fingerprint"`
    FromCache         bool    `json:"from_cache"`
}
```
verdict.Response.Valid() (verdict.go:47-54) is asserted before every write - api.go:178-182 returns 500 {"error":"internal contract violation"} defensively if it ever fails (should be impossible).

POST /v1/verify/bulk - request struct bulkRequest (api.go:190-194):
```
type bulkRequest struct {
    Addresses []string `json:"addresses"`
    Policy    string   `json:"policy,omitempty"`
    CallerRef string   `json:"caller_ref,omitempty"`
}
```
addresses required non-empty (400 if missing/empty, api.go:237-240); capped at bulkAddressCap() - the configured TM_QUEUE_BULK_MAX_ADDRESSES dial if Set, else the built-in constant maxBulkAddresses = 100_000 (api.go:200,204-209) - over-cap returns 413 {"error":"too many addresses","max":N,"got":N}. Body capped at 16<<20 bytes (16MiB, api.go:233). caller_ref is an OPAQUE platform correlation string, never interpreted (api.go:186-194, GAP-36).

Response on 202 Accepted (api.go:260-266):
```json
{"job_id": string, "status": "accepted", "counts": {"total": int, "enqueued": int, "duplicate": int, "malformed": int}}
```

GET /v1/jobs/{id} - no request body; path param id (api.go:281 r.PathValue("id")). Response on 200 (api.go:300-306):
```json
{"job_id": string, "status": string, "complete": bool, "caller_ref": string, "counts": {"total": int, "settled": int, "pending": int}}
```
status is overridden to "complete" when the authoritative completion check (JobCompletion, GAP-38: NOT EXISTS a non-terminal work_item) is true but the stored job.Status is stale (api.go:296-299).

GET /v1/jobs/{id}/results?cursor=&limit= - query params cursor (opaque string, last-seen work_item uuid) and limit (int, default 100, clamped 1..1000, api.go:330-335). Response on 200 (api.go:348-352):
```json
{"job_id": string, "results": [verdict.Response, ...], "next_cursor": string}
```
Each result element is rebuilt via verdictFromRow (api.go:428-451) from the stored VerificationRow - the SAME verdict.Response shape /v1/verify returns, but with two deliberate differences: Email is always "" (plaintext purged on settle per Door 3/DR-4) and Meta carries only Policy/PolicyVersion/FromCache (no request_id/latency/node - those are per-attempt, not job-level).

GET /healthz - no auth, no params. Response 200 always: {"status":"ok"} (api.go:355-357).

GET /readyz - no auth. Response (api.go:361-373): {"ready": bool, "config": string (Config.Summary()), "pepper": "set"|"unset", "supabaseKey": "set"|"unset"}. 200 if ready (pepper loaded), else 503.

The coordinator<->worker interface (control-plane -> verifier-node, internal, NOT the platform boundary) is a separate contract: HTTPClient.VerifyWith POSTs <nodeBaseURL>/v1/verify with body {"email":..., "validation_type":..., "probe_catchall":..., "request_id":...} and raw node-token auth (node/http_client.go:38-85). The Ruby wrapper (verifier-node/truemail-rack/app/truemail_server/wrapper/app.rb) exposes its OWN /v1/verify, /v1/audit, /v1/catchall/:domain, /v1/stats, /v1/config/reload, /v1/config under a URLMap('/v1') mount (wrapper/app.rb:47-56), plus the stock gem's /, /healthcheck, /version at the root (router.rb:23-25). These are coordinator-worker only, per the task's scoping instruction.

categories.name: Error envelope
categories.findings_markdown:
There is NO shared error-envelope constructor/helper. Every handler hand-rolls its own map literal passed to the shared writeJSON(w, code, v) function (api.go:460-464, just json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(v) after setting the status/content-type). The dominant shape across nearly all routes is:
```json
{"error": "<lowercase message>"}
```
using map[string]string{"error": ...} (e.g. api.go:137,145,150,158,164,171,175,180-181,220,224,228,234,238,255,274,278,284,288,293,317,323,326,338).

BUT one route diverges: the bulk over-cap response uses map[string]any (a DIFFERENT shape, three keys, not just "error"):
```json
{"error": "too many addresses", "max": int, "got": int}
```
(api.go:242-244) - this is a distinct error shape from every other route on the same handler.

There are NO error code strings at all (no external_code, no error_code field) - just a free-text "error" message. This is a marked departure from the two-vocabulary rule pattern used elsewhere in this codebase family: no {external code, message, request_id} envelope exists. request_id is never included in any error response body (confirmed by reading every writeJSON call site in api.go - none pass a request_id field).

Distinct shapes found on the platform-facing surface:
1. `{"error": string}` - the overwhelming majority (all of /v1/verify, /healthz implicitly n/a, /v1/jobs/*, most of /v1/verify/bulk).
2. `{"error": string, "max": int, "got": int}` - ONLY the 413 on /v1/verify/bulk (api.go:242-244).
3. Success-shaped map[string]any bodies also vary per route (job status/results/bulk-submit are each bespoke maps, not a shared struct) - not an error shape but shows the whole surface is 'assemble a map ad hoc' rather than typed response structs (except /v1/verify's verdict.Response and job results' embedded verdict.Response array).

HTTP status -> literal message mapping observed (api.go):
- 401 `{"error":"unauthorized"}` (api.go:137,220,274,313)
- 503 `{"error":"service paused"}` (kill-switch FrontDoorReject, api.go:145,224)
- 400 `{"error":"email is required"}` (api.go:150)
- 503 `{"error":"not ready"}` (verifier/policy or bulk/jobs not wired, api.go:158,171,228,278,318)
- 400 `{"error":"unknown policy"}` (api.go:164,248)
- 500 `{"error":"verification failed"}` (api.go:175)
- 500 `{"error":"internal contract violation"}` (defensive Door-1 guard, api.go:180-181)
- 400 `{"error":"invalid request body"}` (api.go:234)
- 400 `{"error":"addresses is required and must be non-empty"}` (api.go:238)
- 413 `{"error":"too many addresses","max":N,"got":N}` (api.go:242-244)
- 500 `{"error":"bulk submit failed"}` (api.go:255)
- 500 `{"error":"job read failed"}` (api.go:284,323)
- 404 `{"error":"job not found"}` (api.go:288,326)
- 500 `{"error":"job status failed"}` (api.go:293)
- 500 `{"error":"job results failed"}` (api.go:338)

All of these are LITERAL lowercase English strings, not codes (no snake_case error-code constants anywhere in api.go). There is no vocab-style frozen error-code enum for HTTP errors comparable to vocab.Status/Reason/Recommendation.

categories.name: Auth mechanism
categories.findings_markdown:
Header: `Authorization`. Scheme: accepts BOTH `Bearer <token>` and a raw token with no scheme prefix - trimBearer (helpers.go:20-28) strips an optional 'Bearer ' prefix via strings.CutPrefix and otherwise returns the header verbatim; there is no rejection of a missing scheme.

Middleware/logic: `(s *Server) authenticate(r *http.Request, requirePerCaller bool) (callerID string, ok bool)` at api.go:386-417. It is called inline at the top of every handler except /healthz and /readyz (not a chained net/http middleware - each handler calls s.authenticate directly).

Three credential types, tried in this precedence:
1. PER-CALLER KEY (PN-13): presented bearer is sha256-hashed (crypto/sha256, api.go:391) and looked up via CallerAuth.LookupCaller(ctx, sha256sum, now) which resolves to store.PG.LookupCaller (postgres.go:1041-1057): `SELECT caller_id FROM api_callers WHERE key_sha256=$1 AND not_before<=$2 AND (not_after IS NULL OR not_after>$2) LIMIT 1`. The key is stored HASHED (key_sha256 bytea, migrations/0010_api_callers.sql:32,39 PRIMARY KEY) - sha256 (fast digest, deliberately NOT a slow KDF per the migration's own comment, since keys are high-entropy brain-issued) rather than a password hash. Comparison is an indexed SQL equality lookup on the hash (not itself constant-time, but keys are high-entropy so no timing-recoverable secret exists in a fast hash lookup - the migration comment explicitly reasons this through, migrations/0010_api_callers.sql:15-21).
2. LEGACY STATIC TOKEN - only accepted when requirePerCaller=false (api.go:399-407): compared via crypto/subtle.ConstantTimeCompare([]byte(presented),[]byte(want)) (api.go:402) - genuinely constant-time. Loaded from secrets.Secrets.FrontDoorToken() (secrets.go:186-191), itself loaded from env var TM_FRONTDOOR_TOKEN (secrets.go:71,106-108) - an env var, not a DB row.
3. DEV OPEN (api.go:411-415) - only when NO per-caller auth wired AND no static token configured AND cfg.Env=="development" - never in production, never on the bulk-PII surface (requirePerCaller=true always fails this branch).

A lookup miss (case 1) falls through to case 2, so a bad per-caller key on a sync call can still match the legacy static token if configured.

Failure returns: 401 `{"error":"unauthorized"}` (uniform across all authenticated routes, api.go:137,220,274,313).

Bulk-PII gate (F-20/PN-13): POST /v1/verify/bulk and BOTH job-read routes call authenticate(r, true) - requirePerCaller=true - which REJECTS the legacy static token entirely (api.go:218,273,313), even if configured and correct. Proven by TestBulkSubmit_StaticTokenRejectedOnBulk (bulk_test.go:95-115) and TestAuthOK_PerCallerKeyLifecycle (auth_test.go:55-99), which also proves rotation-overlap (two active keys, same caller_id, overlapping [not_before,not_after) windows) and not_before enforcement (TestAuthOK_NotYetValidKeyRejected, auth_test.go:102-110).

No mTLS, no HMAC-signed requests, no API-key-in-query-param path exists on the platform boundary - Authorization header only.

categories.name: Versioning scheme
categories.findings_markdown:
URL prefix: `/v1/` on every platform verb (POST /v1/verify, POST /v1/verify/bulk, GET /v1/jobs/{id}, GET /v1/jobs/{id}/results) - api.go:116-121. No version header is read or required anywhere in api.go (grep of the file shows no X-Api-Version or Accept-Version handling).

The response body itself carries a version field: verdict.Response.APIVersion (json tag api_version, verdict.go:18), pinned to the constant `const APIVersion = \"v1\"` (verdict.go:13) - 'A breaking change means /v2, never in-place' (verdict.go:12). This is enforced IN CODE: verdict.Response.Valid() (verdict.go:47-54) checks `r.APIVersion == APIVersion` and every response is asserted against Valid() before being written on the sync path (api.go:178-182 - a mismatch triggers a 500 'internal contract violation' rather than shipping a bad version). handleJobResults's verdictFromRow (api.go:439) sets APIVersion via firstNonEmpty(row.APIVersion, \"v1\") - falls back to the literal \"v1\" if the stored row's APIVersion is empty, but there is no runtime check that a bulk result's stored api_version actually equals the constant (no Valid() call in verdictFromRow's call path in handleJobResults - it is not re-validated the way the sync path is).

Additive-only discipline is enforced by TWO mechanisms, both in code:
1. vocab.go's ValidStatus/ValidReason/ValidRecommendation guard sets (vocab.go:79-102) - a value outside the frozen set fails validation; new phase reasons are pre-declared/reserved in the same const block (vocab.go:58-75, e.g. Phase 2/6/7 reasons reserved from Phase 1) so a later phase's addition is additive by construction, never a rename.
2. The DB CHECK constraints in migrations/0001_verifications.sql:61-79 mirror the vocab sets exactly (valid_status, valid_recommendation, valid_reason CHECK IN (...)) - a genuine second enforcement layer at the DB boundary, and later migrations WIDEN CHECK constraints additively rather than editing existing ones (e.g. migrations/0008_rate_budgets_recovering.sql:26-32 explicitly comments 'The CHECK is REPLACED with a superset (adds recovering); every previously-valid value stays' when widening nodes.status).

No test asserts additive-only as a CI gate specifically (no dedicated contract_drift-style test file was found for module 1); the enforcement is structural (the vocab package + mirrored CHECK constraints), not a standalone gate test.

categories.name: Tenant scoping
categories.findings_markdown:
There is a caller-identity concept but it is NOT used to scope any data-read query - this is a real gap worth flagging plainly.

Two SEPARATE fields exist, deliberately kept apart (migrations/0010_api_callers.sql:23-28):
- `caller_id` (text) - the AUTHENTICATED principal, key-derived, resolved by LookupCaller (postgres.go:1041-1057) and stashed on the request context via callerIDKey{} (api.go:60-62,140-142). It is NEVER a column on jobs/work_items/verifications - it lives only in api_callers and the auth path.
- `caller_ref` (text, nullable) - a caller-SUPPLIED, UNTRUSTED correlation string in the request body (bulkRequest.CallerRef json:\"caller_ref,omitempty\", api.go:193), stored on jobs.caller_ref (migrations/0009_work_items_jobs.sql:99-116 CREATE TABLE jobs ... caller_ref text) and echoed back verbatim on GET /v1/jobs/{id} (api.go:304 job.CallerRef) - never interpreted, never validated, never used to filter.

CRITICALLY: handleBulkSubmit resolves callerID from authenticate() but then discards it - `_ = callerID // authenticated principal; rate-limiting/attribution by caller_id is a later dial` (api.go:251). The store's CreateJob (postgres.go:783-798) does NOT take a caller_id parameter and jobs has NO caller_id/owner column at all (migrations/0009_work_items_jobs.sql:99-116 - only id/policy_key/policy_version/status/total_count/settled_count/submitted_at/completed_at/caller_ref).

CONSEQUENCE: handleJobStatus and handleJobResults require ONLY that the presented bearer authenticate as SOME valid caller (authenticate(r, true), api.go:273,313) - there is NO check that the job_id belongs to the authenticated caller_id. GetJob (postgres.go:801-822), JobCompletion (postgres.go:825-841), and ListJobResults (postgres.go:844-892) all filter ONLY `WHERE id=$1` / `WHERE job_id=$1` - no caller_id predicate anywhere in these queries. Any authenticated caller who learns or guesses another caller's job_id (a UUIDv7, time-ordered and NOT cryptographically random - api.go comments confirm idgen.NewV7String, enqueue.go:70,88) can read that job's full results, including domain and verdict signals, via a different caller's own valid key. This is a genuine cross-tenant read gap: no 403/404 differentiation exists for 'exists but not yours' vs 'doesn't exist' because the concept of 'yours' is never checked.

There is NO Postgres RLS anywhere in the schema (grep for 'row level security'/'FORCE ROW' across migrations/ and internal/ returns zero hits) and migrations/0005_grants.sql:112-113 states explicitly: 'Phase 1 uses service-role key only (OQ-20); no RLS (single client = brain). RLS designed if tenant identities appear later.' This confirms by the code's own comment that tenant isolation was never built at the DB layer.

The alternative correlation field for this module, in place of a tenant column, is the caller_id/caller_ref pair described above - but caller_id is authentication-only (not a data-scoping predicate) and caller_ref is an untrusted echo string, so effectively NO tenant scoping exists on read paths.

categories.name: Status / state vocabulary
categories.findings_markdown:
Verdict vocabulary (vocab/vocab.go), frozen additive-only, mirrored in DB CHECK constraints (migrations/0001_verifications.sql):

Status (exactly 4, vocab.go:21-26): `valid`, `invalid`, `risky`, `unknown`.

Recommendation (3, vocab.go:31-35): `send`, `review`, `skip`.

Composability invariant, enforced by vocab.ComposabilityOK (vocab.go:108-119): invalid=>{skip}; valid=>{send,review}; risky=>{review,skip}; unknown=>{review,skip}. invalid+send is structurally forbidden.

Reason (vocab.go:41-75), grouped by the phase that first emits it, all reserved from Phase 1 forward:
- Phase 1 (cheap layers): `invalid_syntax`, `invalid_domain`, `no_mx`, `null_mx`, `dns_error`, `disposable`, `blacklisted_domain`, `blacklisted_mx`, `spam_trap`, `role_account`, `whitelisted`, `provider_no_smtp`, `plausible`, `unknown_error`.
- Phase 2+ (SMTP, reserved in P1): `accepted`, `mailbox_not_found`, `mailbox_full`, `catch_all`, `accept_all`, `greylisted`, `smtp_blocked`, `smtp_timeout`, `smtp_error`, `connection_failed`.
- Phase 6+ (reserved): `external_verified`.
- Phase 7+ (reserved): `historical_bounce`.
All mirrored verbatim in the CHECK constraint valid_reason (migrations/0001_verifications.sql:66-78).

Job state (jobs.status, migrations/0009_work_items_jobs.sql:99-116, CHECK valid_job_status): `submitted`, `running`, `complete`, `complete_with_unknowns`. Surfaced verbatim on GET /v1/jobs/{id} response's status field (api.go:296-302), with an authoritative-completion override that forces the string literal \"complete\" when JobCompletion()'s NOT-EXISTS check is true but the stored status hasn't caught up yet.

Work-item lifecycle (work_items.status, migrations/0009_work_items_jobs.sql:35-71, CHECK valid_work_item_status): `ready`, `in_flight`, `waiting_retry`, `settled`, `dead` - NOT surfaced directly on the platform boundary (only the aggregate job counts/completion derived from it are exposed).

Node lifecycle (nodes.status, migrations/0003_lists_nodes_policies.sql:61-68 valid_status, WIDENED additively by migrations/0008_rate_budgets_recovering.sql:24-32): `provisioning`, `active`, `quarantined`, `recovering` (recovering added in 0008 as a superset CHECK replacement). Node audit_status (migrations/0007_node_audits_warmup.sql:31-36 valid_audit_status): `green`, `red`. NEITHER of these node states is exposed on the platform-facing routes at all (no /v1 route returns node status) - they are purely internal to the health-watcher control loop (internal/health/decide.go's Lifecycle* constants, decide.go:40-45, mirrors these strings without importing the audit package).

mx_provider classification (verifications.mx_provider, promoted typed column, migrations/0001_verifications.sql:37-39 comment): `google`, `o365`, `yahoo`, `self`, `other` - derived by internal/layers/dns_layers.go's providerMXSuffixes (dns_layers.go:54-81), surfaced as part of verdict Signals/flags on /v1/verify and echoed in bulk results' domain grouping context.

Health-watcher Action.Reason strings (health/decide.go:109, not on the platform boundary, internal only): `audit_red`, `liveness`, `block_rate`, `canary_recover`, `canary_reblock`, `fleet_brake_hold`, `active_floor_hold`, `canary_start`.

categories.name: Cost / feasibility expression
categories.findings_markdown:
There is NO pre-flight/quote verb and NO cost or feasibility field anywhere on the platform-facing surface. Confirmed by exhaustive review of every request/response struct in api.go, verdict.go, and store.go: verifyRequest has only email/policy; bulkRequest has only addresses/policy/caller_ref; the 202 response has only job_id/status/counts(total,enqueued,duplicate,malformed); the job-status/results responses have no cost/credit/price fields.

The ONLY numeric 'cost' concept in the entire codebase is `cost_units` on the internal external_calls table (migrations/0011_external_calls.sql, referenced in store/postgres.go:965-979 insertExternalCallTx, columns c.CostUnits) - this is an OPERATOR-side spend-tracking ledger for the Phase-6 third-party-vendor fallback layer (budget ceilings ExternalDailyCap/ExternalMonthlyCap/ExternalPerJobCap in config.go:196-199), used purely for the internal circuit-breaker/budget enforcement (config.go ExternalFallbackEnabled, configToBudget in main.go:315-322). It is NEVER exposed to a platform caller - no route reads or returns cost_units, no request accepts a budget parameter, and the vendor adapter itself (external.Vendor) is not even wired to a real vendor in this phase (main.go:239-280, 'PENDING-REAL-VENDOR').

There is also no 'feasibility' verb - the closest analogue is that /v1/verify ITSELF is the only way to learn anything about an address, and it always executes the real (cheap-layer, and later SMTP) pipeline rather than a dry-run/estimate mode; there is no 'would this succeed' probe distinct from actually running it. The bulk submission's 202 response's counts.total/enqueued/duplicate/malformed (api.go:262-265) is the closest thing to a pre-execution signal, but it reports what WAS accepted into the queue post-normalization, not a cost or a feasibility prediction - it is a post-hoc accounting of the submission itself, computed AFTER work-items are created (enqueue.go:75-135), not a pre-flight estimate before committing to the work.

Bottom line: this module offers no quote-equivalent whatsoever. A platform caller learns 'cost' only by submitting real work (sync verify or bulk submit) and observing the counts/verdicts that come back; there is no currency, no unit-price, no dry-run flag, no estimated-duration field on any platform route.
evidence: control-plane/internal/api/api.go:127-267 (verifyRequest, bulkRequest, all response shapes - no cost/feasibility field)
control-plane/internal/config/config.go:183-199 (External*Cap dials are operator-side budget ceilings, never surfaced)
control-plane/cmd/control-plane/main.go:232-281 (buildExternal - PENDING-REAL-VENDOR, no real cost path exists even internally)

categories.name: Admin surface + its auth
categories.findings_markdown:
There is NO operator/admin HTTP route anywhere in this module. Exhaustive search: grep for 'adminapi', '/admin', 'X-Admin', 'AdminKey', 'platform_admin' across control-plane and verifier-node returns zero hits. The Handler() mux (api.go:114-125) registers exactly six routes, all already covered in category 1 - four platform verbs plus /healthz and /readyz (which are unauthenticated but not 'admin' - they carry no secret values, only presence booleans and a config summary string).

Route count: 0 dedicated admin HTTP routes. There is exactly one Go binary (cmd/control-plane/main.go - confirmed the only file with func main in the whole repo) and it serves only the six routes above; there is no separate admin server, no CLI subcommand for key issuance visible in the codebase (no cobra/flag-based admin tool found under control-plane/cmd beyond the single main.go).

Instead, every 'admin' action in this module is a DIRECT DATABASE OPERATION performed under the cp_admin Postgres role (migrations/0005_grants.sql:22-31), which is explicitly NOT the runtime's own login role (cp_runtime) - it is a break-glass, admin-audited credential distinct from the app's DB credential. Concretely:
- Per-caller key issuance/rotation (api_callers INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE) is cp_admin-only; cp_runtime gets SELECT only (migrations/0010_api_callers.sql:56-60) - so a platform key is minted by an operator running SQL/a migration-adjacent tool directly against Postgres, never through an HTTP admin endpoint.
- Node registration/lifecycle mutation is either done via UpsertNodeState/SetNodeStatus store methods called from main.go's startup wiring (main.go:433-440) or the internal health-watcher control loop (health/decide.go, run by startHealthWatcher, main.go:478-514) - not by any admin HTTP call.
- Policy definitions are seeded via EnsurePolicy at startup (main.go:122-126) from a code-embedded JSON (policy.ColdEmailDefinitionJSON), not via an admin write route.

Since there is no admin HTTP surface, there is also no shared-vs-separate-credential question to resolve for THIS module (the platform credential is the Authorization bearer/per-caller key described in category 3; the 'admin' credential is a raw Postgres role, a wholly different trust boundary, never presented over HTTP at all). There is consequently no 'parallel write path' HTTP route to flag either - the only parallel write path is direct SQL access under cp_admin, which is architecturally separate from (and cannot be confused with) the platform's HTTP write paths (POST /v1/verify, POST /v1/verify/bulk).
evidence: control-plane/internal/api/api.go:114-125 (only 6 routes exist, no admin route)
control-plane/cmd/control-plane/main.go:118-126,433-440,478-514 (node/policy mutation via startup wiring or the health-watcher loop, not HTTP)

categories.name: Health / observability
categories.findings_markdown:
Liveness/readiness (platform-facing, api.go):
- GET /healthz (api.go:355-357): no dependency check at all. Always 200, body `{\"status\":\"ok\"}`.
- GET /readyz (api.go:361-373): computes `ready := s.secrets != nil && s.secrets.HasPepper()`. Returns 200 if ready, else 503 (StatusServiceUnavailable). Body:
```json
{"ready": bool, "config": "<Config.Summary() string>", "pepper": "set"|"unset", "supabaseKey": "set"|"unset"}
```
config is a free-text summary string, NOT structured JSON, from Config.Summary() (config.go:820-828): `\"env=%s listen=%s ladder=%s smtp=%s fallback=%s frontdoor=%s nodes=%d mutators=recommend-only\"`. Note: readiness reports the kill-switch RUNG (config.go:822-825 rung=\"full\"|\"cheap-layers-only(Rung3)\") but is not gated on DB/verifier wiring - a control-plane can report ready=true (pepper loaded) while /v1/verify itself is separately 503 for lack of a wired verifier/DB (api.go:157-160) - readyz and /v1/verify's own not-ready check are NOT the same test.

Metrics: there is NO /metrics endpoint and NO Prometheus client library in go.mod (only jackc/pgx/v5, golang.org/x/net, golang.org/x/text - confirmed by reading control-plane/go.mod in full). Grep for 'prometheus' or a literal '/metrics' route across the whole Go tree returns zero route/library hits. The internal/metrics package (metrics/metrics.go) is a PURE, in-process derivation function (Derive(rows []store.MetricRow, truncated bool) Snapshot, metrics.go:67-133) that computes BlockRatePoolWide/UnknownRate/CacheHitRate/LatencyP50/95/99/PerNode/PerProvider/RateLimitedCount from a caller-supplied window of LOG rows - it has NO HTTP exposure, no scrape endpoint, no exporter wiring anywhere (grep for 'metrics.Derive(' outside the metrics package/tests returns nothing that wires it to an HTTP handler). It exists purely as a library any future dashboard/exporter COULD call, but nothing in this codebase currently does.

Structured logging: uses Go's stdlib log package only (`log.SetFlags(log.LstdFlags | log.LUTC)`, main.go:37) - plain-text timestamped lines via log.Printf/log.Fatalf, NOT JSON, NOT a structured logger (no zap/zerolog/logrus in go.mod). No request_id or correlation id is emitted in any log.Printf call site reviewed (main.go's ~30 log.Printf calls are all human-readable prose, e.g. main.go:43,52,78,102,113 etc.) - request_id exists only inside the DB row (VerificationRow.RequestID, stored via the LOG insert) and the response Meta.request_id field, never threaded into the process's stdout/stderr logs. Secrets are explicitly redacted before logging: secrets.Secrets.String() (secrets.go:194-199) renders only <set>/<unset> tokens, and main.go:52 logs sec.String() (never a raw secret) - confirmed no log.Printf call site in main.go or api.go prints a token/key/pepper value directly.

categories.name: DB boundary
categories.findings_markdown:
Schema: no explicit CREATE SCHEMA statement was found (tables are created without a schema-qualifying prefix, e.g. `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS verifications (...)` in migrations/0001_verifications.sql:9 - they land in whatever schema is default/search_path, typically `public` on a bare Postgres/Supabase instance). This is architecturally different from the sibling modules' explicit `byosmtp`-style dedicated schema.

Roles (migrations/0005_grants.sql:9-31): TWO NOLOGIN roles are created via idempotent DO $$ blocks - `cp_runtime` (comment: 'maps to Supabase service_role concept... Gets INSERT+SELECT only on verifications') and `cp_admin` ('Grant-admin / DDL owner. Separate break-glass, admin-audited credential'). Both are NOLOGIN roles at creation (0005_grants.sql:15,26) - the actual login/connection identity in Supabase deployment is the service_role key (mapped in a comment, 0005_grants.sql:108-113), not a first-class Postgres LOGIN role defined in these migrations; this differs from an explicit CREATE ROLE ... LOGIN pattern.

Grants are issued PER-TABLE, individually enumerated (never a blanket default-privileges ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES statement) - e.g. migrations/0005_grants.sql:38-102 grants GRANT SELECT,INSERT ON verifications TO cp_runtime; REVOKE UPDATE,DELETE ON verifications FROM cp_runtime; GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON verifications TO cp_admin; and separately for verification_raw + its date partitions, cache, catchall_domains/disposable_domains/spam_trap_domains, nodes, policies, send_outcomes, verification_outcomes. Every subsequent migration that adds a table follows the same per-table GRANT/REVOKE pattern explicitly (migrations/0006_catchall_write.sql grants cp_runtime INSERT+UPDATE on catchall_domains; migrations/0007_node_audits_warmup.sql grants cp_runtime INSERT+SELECT on node_audits, SELECT+INSERT+UPDATE on node_warmup; migrations/0008_rate_budgets_recovering.sql grants cp_runtime SELECT+INSERT+UPDATE on rate_budgets; migrations/0010_api_callers.sql:58-60 grants cp_runtime SELECT ONLY on api_callers, explicitly REVOKEs INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE from cp_runtime). This IS the append-only/least-privilege enforcement mechanism for 'THE LOG' (verifications) - cp_runtime structurally cannot UPDATE or DELETE a logged verdict.

RLS is NOT used anywhere: grep for 'row level security'/'FORCE ROW' across the whole migrations/ and internal/ directories returns zero matches. migrations/0005_grants.sql:112-113 states this explicitly as a deliberate Phase-1 decision: 'Phase 1 uses service-role key only (OQ-20); no RLS (single client = brain). RLS designed if tenant identities appear later.' - i.e. RLS was considered and deferred, not merely omitted.

Which services hold DB credentials: only the Go control-plane (via store.OpenPG(ctx, cfg.DatabaseURL), main.go:109) holds a Postgres connection string (TM_DATABASE_URL env var, config.go:239,534-536) and it uses the cp_runtime-equivalent credential (Supabase service_role key per the comment). The Ruby verifier-node (truemail-rack fork) is structurally DB-less: no Postgres/database gem dependency was found in its app/config directories during this review, and its wrapper endpoints (app.rb) never reference a DB connection - confirming the coordinator (control-plane) holds all DB access and the worker (verifier-node) structurally cannot reach the database, matching this module's own Door-5 ('dumb box; all interpretation control-plane-side') design note in node/audit_client.go:14-16.

categories.name: Config approach
categories.findings_markdown:
Mechanism: environment variables ONLY, loaded via config.Load(getenv func(string) string) (config.go:525-732), with config.LoadFromOS() (config.go:735) as the production entrypoint reading os.Getenv. There is NO DB-backed config table for tunables (unlike the sibling module's byosmtp.config JSONB-row pattern) - config.go:16-19's own package comment states the precedence is 'built-in safe defaults -> config file (YAML/JSON, added at P1) -> environment overrides' but no file-based loader was found implemented; only Defaults() (config.go:432-520) + env overrides (Load, config.go:525-732) exist in code.

Key count: the Dials struct (config.go:121-226) alone declares ~50 individual tunables spanning P1 cache/recommendation thresholds through P7 flywheel recalibration guards (CacheTTLSeconds, RawBlobRetentionDays, RecommendationSend/Review, SMTPClientDeadlineMS, AuditMaxAgeSeconds, WarmupDailyCap, WatcherCadenceSeconds, BlockRateWindowSeconds, BlockMinSamples, BlockQuarThresholdPct, BlockRecoverThreshPct, CanaryRecoverGreens, CanaryMinSamples, CanarySampleN, LivenessMisses, FleetWidePct, CanaryWarmupCap, PoolEligibleFloor, RateSaturationCount, QueueBackoffBaseSeconds/Factor/CapSeconds/JitterPct, QueueRateWaitSeconds, QueueMaxAttempts, QueueMaxRetryAgeSeconds, QueueLeaseMarginSeconds, QueueDrainBatchSize, QueueDrainIdlePollSeconds, QueueBulkMaxAddresses, ExternalDailyCap/MonthlyCap/PerJobCap/RateCeiling, ExternalErrorRatePct/MinSamples/BreakerCooldownSeconds, HistoricalBounceTTLDays/MinN/Penalty, RecalMinBucketSamples/MaxStep/UpStepPct/BrakeWindowCycles/BrakeBucketPct/BrakeMinBuckets/CadenceSeconds) plus the KillSwitch (SMTP/Fallback/FrontDoor modes) and ShadowModes (4 mode dials) structs and top-level Config booleans (FlywheelGateEnabled, FlywheelCalibrationEnabled, ExternalDPAConfirmed) - well over 60 distinct readable settings in total. Every env var is prefixed TM_ (e.g. TM_ENV, TM_LISTEN_ADDR, TM_DATABASE_URL, TM_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS, TM_SMTP_MODE, TM_QUEUE_BULK_MAX_ADDRESSES, etc. - config.go:528-729).

Hot-reloadability: NONE on the control-plane side - config is loaded once at process start (main.go:39) and never re-read; a change requires a process restart. (The Ruby verifier-node DOES have a hot-reload verb, POST /v1/config/reload at wrapper/app.rb:148-160, but that is the coordinator-worker interface, not the platform boundary, and only affects the engine wrapper's own config, not the control-plane's.)

Owner-OQ 'Dial' pattern: several dials use a `Dial{Value int; Set bool}` wrapper (config.go:106-116) so an unset dial is DISTINGUISHABLE from an explicit zero - e.g. CacheTTLSeconds, SMTPClientDeadlineMS, QueueBulkMaxAddresses, the four External*Cap dials - each explicitly defaults to `Dial{Set: false}` (config.go:450,454,491,497-500) rather than a guessed value, and consuming code (e.g. CacheTTL(), config.go:358-363) returns a 'do nothing' zero-duration when Set is false, refusing to invent a value.

CI gate against hardcoded constants: no dedicated CI gate/test (e.g. no 'no_hardcoded_constant' grep-based test file) was found for this module (unlike a sibling module's named config_drift/no_secret_leak gates) - the discipline is enforced by convention/comments (e.g. config.go's extensive inline comments explaining why each Dial is settable) rather than an automated lint step in .github/workflows/ci.yml (reviewed in full; jobs are control-plane build/vet/test, door5-gem-unmodified, verifier-node-rspec, docs-discipline, code-review - none of these greps for literal tuning constants).

Hardcoded tuning literals actually found in RUNTIME (non-test) code, despite the 'config not code' discipline:
- api.go:200 `const maxBulkAddresses = 100_000` - the built-in safe hard cap used ONLY when the TM_QUEUE_BULK_MAX_ADDRESSES dial is unset (api.go:204-209) - a genuine runtime-behavior-governing literal, though the code frames it as a documented fallback rather than a silent magic number.
- api.go:149 `1<<16` (64KiB body cap on /v1/verify) and api.go:233 `16<<20` (16MiB body cap on /v1/verify/bulk) - hardcoded, not config-driven.
- api.go:330-335: results pagination `limit := 100` default, clamped to `n <= 1000` - both hardcoded, not config keys.
- node/http_client.go:32 `deadline = 15 * time.Second` - the node client's fallback deadline when the caller passes <=0.
- cmd/control-plane/main.go:73 `ReadHeaderTimeout: 5 * time.Second` and main.go:214 `maxSMTP = 60 * time.Second` (fallback when the SMTPClientDeadlineMS dial is unset).
- node/*.go: several `io.LimitReader(resp.Body, 1<<20)` / `1<<16` response-body caps (audit_client.go:45, config_client.go:42, health_client.go:43, http_client.go:77) - all hardcoded byte-size ceilings, never config keys.
None of these have a corresponding TM_* env var or Dials field - they are genuine, if arguably minor/defensible, exceptions to the 'no hardcoded tuning constants' rule stated in this family's build discipline.

categories.name: Migration conventions
categories.findings_markdown:
File naming: `NNNN_description.sql` with a 4-digit zero-padded sequence prefix (e.g. 0001_verifications.sql, 0002_cache.sql, ... 0012_flywheel_calibration.sql) - a SINGLE .sql file per migration, NOT split into separate .up.sql/.down.sql files. There is no down/rollback file for ANY migration (confirmed: `ls control-plane/migrations` shows only 0001..0012 plus README.md - no *_down.sql or *.down.sql variants exist). This is explicitly a forward-only convention: migrations/README.md states 'Forward-only SQL DDL translating the approved Phase-1 spec' and additive changes are done via CHECK-constraint REPLACEMENT within the SAME forward file (e.g. migrations/0008_rate_budgets_recovering.sql:24-32 drops and recreates the nodes.status CHECK as a superset, all inside one forward-only migration) rather than a paired down migration undoing an up migration.

Runner: no bespoke Go/custom migration-runner binary was found in the codebase (no internal/migrate package, no `migrate` subcommand under cmd/). CI applies migrations with a plain shell loop over psql (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:44-51`): `for f in $(ls migrations/[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]_*.sql | sort); do PGPASSWORD=ci psql ... -f "$f"; done` - i.e. the 'runner' is literally `sort` + sequential `psql -f`, relying on filename lexical order, with NO tracking table (no schema_migrations/applied_migrations table was found in any migration file) - re-running the same migration twice would rely entirely on each file's own `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` / idempotent `DO $$ ... IF NOT EXISTS` guards (e.g. migrations/0005_grants.sql:12-18,23-29) rather than a runner-enforced 'already applied' ledger.

Manual apply instructions in migrations/README.md also show three alternative paths: local Docker Postgres (`for f in control-plane/migrations/*.sql; do psql ... -f "$f"; done`), the Supabase Dashboard SQL Editor (paste + execute each file), or Supabase CLI's `supabase db push` - none of which imply a dedicated runner tool either; they all lean on the same idempotent-DDL + lexical-order convention.

Migration lint gate: NONE found. No CI job or script named migration_lint (or equivalent) exists; grep across scripts/, .github/workflows/, and Docs/ for 'migration.*lint' returns zero hits for this module (the phrase only exists in an unrelated sibling module's docs, which per the task's own instruction is not evidence for this module). The only migration-adjacent CI safeguard is the ci.yml `apply migrations` step itself (lines 44-51), which will fail the whole 'control-plane' job if any file in sequence errors out (`ON_ERROR_STOP=1`) - a correctness check, not a style/lint gate.

categories.name: Kill switches and shadow modes
categories.findings_markdown:
This module has a genuine GRADUATED LADDER, not merely a single on/off, plus a separate per-mutator shadow-mode system - both are first-class config (config.go), not hardcoded.

Kill-switch ladder (config.go:32-76), each rung independently a config field:
- Rung 1 (SMTP): `KillSwitch.SMTP` (type SMTPMode) values `"enabled"`/`"disabled"` (config.go:41-44). Default `SMTPDisabled` (config.go:439). Env override `TM_SMTP_MODE` (config.go:554-556, no validation of the string beyond Validate()'s switch at config.go:740-744 which rejects any value outside the two). Read by Config.SMTPEnabled() (config.go:298) and gates whether buildSMTP even attempts to wire the SMTP stage (main.go:353).
- Rung 2 (Fallback / 'Global A'): `KillSwitch.Fallback` (type FallbackMode) values `"enabled"`/`"off"` (config.go:49-52). Default `FallbackOff` (config.go:440). Env `TM_FALLBACK_MODE` (config.go:557-559). Read by ExternalFallbackEnabled() (config.go:281-283, ANDed with ExternalDPAConfirmed) and directly checked as the 'global-fallback-kill' override in buildExternal (main.go:245-253).
- Rung 3 (cheap-layers-only): NOT its own field - a DERIVED state, `KillSwitch.CheapLayersOnly()` (config.go:74-76) = SMTP disabled AND Fallback off. This is the default/steady-state at Phase 1 (config.go:436-441 comment: 'the honest, SAFE default IS cheap-layers-only').
- Rung 4 (front door): `KillSwitch.FrontDoor` (type FrontDoorMode) THREE values (config.go:57-61): `"serving"` (default, config.go:441), `"accept_and_defer"`, `"reject"`. Env `TM_FRONTDOOR_MODE` (config.go:560-562). Read directly in the HTTP handlers: api.go:144 and api.go:223 both check `s.cfg.KillSwitch.FrontDoor == config.FrontDoorReject` and short-circuit to 503 `{"error":"service paused"}` BEFORE any body parsing - this is the only rung with a DIRECT platform-facing effect visible in the handler code (the accept_and_defer value is declared but no handler branch was found consuming it distinctly from 'serving' - it appears to be a reserved/future value, api.go grep shows only the FrontDoorReject branch wired).

Shadow-mode dials (config.go:83-98, DR-2), each an independent Mode (`"shadow"`/`"recommend_only"`/`"auto"`) - four named mutators, ALL default `ModeRecommendOnly` (config.go:443-448):
- A1BlockRateQuarantine - read by main.go:493-496 (`blockMode := health.ModeRecommendOnly; if cfg.ShadowModes.A1BlockRateQuarantine == config.ModeAuto { blockMode = health.ModeAuto }`) and consumed inside health/decide.go's Evaluate() (decide.go:241-248): at recommend_only, a block-rate trip produces ONLY an Action{Apply:false, Recommend:"QUARANTINE-ELIGIBLE..."} - zero live mutation - matching this module family's DR-2 fresh-system invariant.
- A6ConfidenceRecalib, A8ProviderPromotion, A9FallbackWeaning - declared, defaulted recommend_only, VALIDATED (config.go:754-764 rejects any mode string outside shadow/recommend_only/auto) but no consuming code site for A8/A9 was found wired to a live mechanism in this phase (they are declared-but-not-yet-consumed dials per the config.go comment at line 97: 'A2/A3/A4/A5/A7/A10/A11 stay auto/alert per shadow-mode... not owner dials here').

Separate opt-in flags (default FALSE, i.e. shadow-mode-by-default in spirit): `FlywheelGateEnabled` (config.go:245-249, historical-bounce gate), `FlywheelCalibrationEnabled` (config.go:250-254, calibrated-confidence read), `ExternalDPAConfirmed` (config.go:260-268, legal DPA gate for vendor egress) - each requires the LITERAL string "true" via env (TM_FLYWHEEL_GATE_ENABLED, TM_FLYWHEEL_CALIBRATION_ENABLED, TM_EXTERNAL_DPA_CONFIRMED at config.go:717,724,727) - all off by default, all requiring explicit operator action to enable, and ExternalFallbackEnabled() (config.go:281-283) requires BOTH the Fallback rung AND the DPA flag before the external layer can even be considered live - a genuine multi-switch 'enabling is hard' design (main.go:232-280 additionally requires a vendor key present, and even then refuses to wire a real vendor this phase - 'PENDING-REAL-VENDOR', main.go:275-280).

So: YES, a real ladder (4 named rungs, one derived) exists, is entirely config-driven (env-var overridable), and is validated at load (config.go:739-817 Validate() rejects illegal mode strings and several unsafe numeric combinations, e.g. FleetWidePct must be 1..99 or the fleet-wide brake becomes mathematically unable to fire, config.go:777-787). Shadow-mode-by-default is real for A1 and for the two Flywheel/DPA opt-ins - not merely one on/off switch.

categories.name: Logging discipline
categories.findings_markdown:
There is no dedicated automated CI gate/test file specifically named for a 'no secret in logs' rule in this module (no no_secret_leak-style test/script was found under control-plane/ or scripts/ for module 1 specifically - that phrase only appears associated with a different module's docs, which per the task's own instructions is not evidence here).

What DOES exist as an in-code discipline: secrets.Secrets.String() (secrets.go:193-199) is explicitly written to redact everything - it renders each secret as `<set>`/`<unset>` via the redact() helper (secrets.go:201-206) and only counts nodeTokens/vendorKeys (lengths, not values): `Secrets{pepper:<set> supabase:<set> frontdoor:<unset> queueAddr:<set> queueAddrPrev:<unset> nodeTokens:2 vendorKeys:0}`-shaped output. The package doc comment for secrets.go (lines 1-4) states 'nothing here is ever written to disk, logged, or committed' as an explicit design intent. main.go:52 logs exactly this redacted String(), never a raw secret.

Manual review of every log.Printf/log.Fatalf call site in cmd/control-plane/main.go (the only file with logging calls of consequence) found NO instance where a token, key, pepper, or password value is interpolated directly - every secret-adjacent log line either logs presence/absence (main.go:62,102,113,186,262) or an env-var NAME (main.go:186 `secrets.EnvQueueAddrKey`, main.go:262 `secrets.EnvVendorKeys`) rather than its value. No raw DB error string is logged either in a way that could leak a DSN's password - store errors are wrapped with fmt.Errorf("store: ...: %w", err) (e.g. postgres.go:795,816,832) and main.go logs `err` via `%v` at the OpenPG failure site (main.go:113 `log.Printf("verify: store unavailable (%v)...", err)`) - this COULD in principle include a Postgres connection error message; pgx v5 error messages for connection failures typically do not embed the DSN password verbatim, but this was not independently verified against pgx's exact error-formatting behavior, so it is flagged as a residual risk rather than a confirmed leak.

No ciphertext or ciphertext-adjacent value (e.g. ADR-0002/DR-4's addr_ciphertext, or a node token) was found interpolated into any log.Printf call in main.go or the queue/node packages during this review - queue.Enqueuer/Drainer methods do not appear to log the plaintext-address argument directly (only the derived IDs/counts). This is consistent with, but not exhaustively proven by, a dedicated log-scanning test - no such test exists in this codebase for module 1.

categories.name: Tests
categories.findings_markdown:
Platform-boundary routes are tested with REAL net/http/httptest requests against the ACTUAL mux (srv.Handler().ServeHTTP), never a mocked router - api_test.go and bulk_test.go and auth_test.go all build a real *api.Server and drive it through httptest.NewRecorder()/httptest.NewRequest. The DEPENDENCIES behind the handler are injected via interfaces (Verifier, CallerAuth, BulkSubmitter, JobReader in api.go:34-58) so unit-style tests (api_test.go) use store.NewMem (an in-memory fake store, store/mem.go) for speed, while the STORE layer itself is separately tested against REAL Postgres: internal/store/postgres_test.go gates on `TM_TEST_DATABASE_URL` and calls `t.Skip("PENDING: set TM_TEST_DATABASE_URL to a migrated Postgres to exercise the real store (never faked)")` when unset (postgres_test.go:26-28) - matching this module family's 'never fake behavioral tests, skip honestly' convention. CI wires this for real: .github/workflows/ci.yml:26-58 spins up a genuine `postgres:16-alpine` service container, applies every migration file via psql in lexical order, then runs `go test -v ./...` WITH `TM_TEST_DATABASE_URL` set - so the Postgres-backed tests actually RUN in CI, not just locally.

Key test files: internal/api/api_test.go (219 lines - sync /v1/verify contract, auth-in-production, readyz-reflects-pepper), internal/api/auth_test.go (125 lines - per-caller key lifecycle, rotation overlap, F-20 bulk gate), internal/api/bulk_test.go (225 lines - bulk submit auth gate, static-token-rejected-on-bulk, full submit->drain->status->results end-to-end lifecycle through real HTTP + a real queue.Drainer + real queue.AddrCipher), internal/store/postgres_test.go (real-Postgres store integration, incl. append-only grant enforcement: postgres_test.go:398 skips the DELETE-should-fail assertion when 'connected as a privileged role (DELETE allowed)' - itself evidence the test suite is aware of and checks for role-privilege correctness rather than assuming it), internal/store/postgres_flywheel_test.go, internal/queue/pg_e2e_test.go (real end-to-end queue-vs-Postgres), internal/vocab/vocab_test.go, internal/health/decide_test.go, internal/config/config_test.go.

Paired positive/negative control convention: consistently present and explicitly documented as such. Concrete example: TestAuthOK_PerCallerKeyLifecycle (auth_test.go:55-99) has an explicit 'FAIL-VERIFY' comment block (auth_test.go:50-54) stating exactly what code change would make the test fail: 'remove the now in [not_before, not_after) window from LookupCaller -> the rotated-out case starts authenticating -> this test fails' and 'make the bulk path call authenticate(r, false) instead of true -> the static-token-rejected-on-bulk case fails' - i.e. the test author reasoned through and documented the specific mutation that breaks the property, and the test body then asserts BOTH the positive case (active-key/rot-old/rot-new authenticate, lines 69,81,84,96) and the negative controls (unknown key rejected line 73, expired/rotated-out key rejected line 77, not-yet-valid key rejected in the separate TestAuthOK_NotYetValidKeyRejected at lines 102-110, legacy-static-rejected-on-bulk line 92-94) in the SAME test function so the control and the property are verified together. TestVerifyInvalidNeverSaysSend (api_test.go:101-114) is a similarly-paired guard: asserts BOTH that a no-MX address IS classified invalid/no_mx (the positive) AND that recommendation is never 'send' for it (the negative/forbidden-combination control, explicitly commented 'FORBIDDEN: invalid recommended send (Door 1)').

No mock-the-DB test stands in for the append-only/CAS/idempotency behavioral properties per this module's own real-infra discipline (mirrored from the sibling modules' Rule 3) - the store package's PG-suffixed tests are the ones proving exactly-once settlement/append-only grants, and they SKIP (never fake-pass) without a real Postgres.

uncertainties: The DB error-message leak question in category 14 (pgx connection-failure error text potentially embedding DSN fragments when logged via %v at main.go:113) was not independently verified against pgx v5's exact error-formatting behavior — flagged as a residual risk, not a confirmed leak.

No dedicated CI gate named 'migration_lint', 'config_drift', 'contract_drift', 'config_consumption', 'drain_grace', or 'no_secret_leak' (the six-gate naming convention referenced in this repo's own CLAUDE.md for a DIFFERENT module) was found anywhere in module 1's codebase or CI workflow — module 1 appears to predate or simply never adopt that gate-naming convention; this is reported as an absence, not assumed to be a gap in coverage.

Docs/config-manifest.md and other Docs/*.md files were used only for orientation (per the task's explicit instruction) and were NOT used as evidence for any claim in this report — all category findings are traced to actual .go/.sql/.rb source. Where a doc and the code might disagree, no such disagreement was specifically hunted for beyond the RLS note in migrations/0005_grants.sql, which is itself code (a SQL comment), not a separate doc file.

It was not verified with 100% certainty that no other Go binary/entrypoint exists anywhere in the repo (searched for every 'func main' occurrence and found exactly one, in cmd/control-plane/main.go); this is treated as conclusive given the grep result but flagged since the search was tool-based rather than an exhaustive manual directory read.

The verifier-node (Ruby) side was deliberately scoped 'only briefly' per the task instructions; its own auth (AccessToken service), config loader, and full route surface were not exhaustively read beyond confirming the /v1/verify, /v1/audit, /v1/catchall/:domain, /v1/stats, /v1/config/reload, /v1/config routes and the stock /, /healthcheck, /version routes — deeper Ruby-side details (e.g. exact AccessToken comparison method) were not verified and are not claimed here.
